figures.caption: Figure 1: Predictor construction changes multimodal neural contrasts. (A) In Places, ∆V (L) decreases with text length. The original one-caption versus narrative contrast (dashed arrow) favors the narrative but reverses when four captions approximately match narrative length. Open orange points are caption-length narrative truncations; grey diamonds are content-destroyed controls. (B) Length matching shifts every ROI in both subjects toward the caption predictor. Only Places and V1 in subj01 cross zero, but all matched-length contrasts are negative. Filled/open markers indicate subj01/subj02; error bars are 95% bootstrap intervals. (C) Decomposition of the Places contrast into changes in joint prediction, r(V+L), and language-only prediction, r(L). The language-only term is larger in magnitude in both subjects and comparisons.
